chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Abu Sa'id al-Ahwal, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the minimum amount for the dowry of temporary marriage (mut'ah)?' He said, 'A handful of wheat.'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: Temporary marriage (mut'ah), a form of marriage with a specified duration.
key_terms.بُرٍّ: Wheat (specifically the grain itself, used here as a measure of value).
key_terms.كَفٌّ: A handful (the amount held in the cupped hand).

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum dowry required for temporary marriage (mut'ah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the minimum legal dowry (mahr) for temporary marriage (mut'ah) as 'a handful of wheat,' emphasizing the accessibility and flexibility of the contract. This nominal value underscores the Shia juristic view that mut'ah is a valid, distinct marital form requiring only a minimal material component to be legally binding, distinguishing it from permanent marriage where higher dowries are often customary.
